newsitem.title: BERMUDA: RUGBY UNION - McLeod injury latest blow for Chiefs.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - McLeod injury latest blow for Chiefs.

text.p: HAMILTON, March 18 - A training injury to in-form player Scott McLeod has left the Waikato Chiefs backline decimated for this Saturday night's Super 12 rugby match against Queensland.
NZPA reports McLeod suffered a suspected ruptured disc in his back doing squats during weight training yesterday and is expected to be out for a minimum of three weeks.

He joins other backs Matthew Cooper, who strained medial ligaments in his right knee in the match against Auckland Blues in Albany on Saturday night, and World Cup Sevens players Glen Osborne, Eric Rush and Caleb Ralph as unavailable for the Rugby Park match against the Queensland Reds. There is an outside
chance Cooper may recover in time.

McLeod played on the left wing for the Chiefs in the absence of the sevens players and scored their only try against the Blues, while he made huge impact at second five-eighths against both the New South Wales Waratahs and the Wellington Hurricanes.
"Scott's flat on his back today and will be out for a minimum of three weeks and maybe up to six weeks," Chiefs manager Steve Gilbert said today.
Chiefs coach Brad Meurant said it was devastating news: "But we've just got to keep our heads, work through the processes and get the best team on the track that is possible."

Meurant, who will name the team to play Queensland on Thursday morning, also faces problems in his forward pack, having lost tighthead prop Richard Loe for the next two games through suspension and blind-side flanker Blair Larsen for three to four weeks with a stress fracture in his ankle.

No 8 Deon Muir (ankle) and flanker/lock Richard Coventry (groin) have missed the first three Super 12 games. Muir, who was getting a second specialist's opinion on his ankle today, and Coventry face fitness tests when the team resume training in Hamilton tomorrow afternoon.
Wellington's Mike Edwards has been called in as a temporary replacement for Loe, although Lee Lidgard is likely to start against Queensland.

Bay of Plenty's Damon Kaui has been brought in to cover for Cooper, Waikato flanker Aaron Hopa comes in for Larsen and Meurant and assistant coach John Boe will consider a further replacement for McLeod tomorrow after Cooper tests his knee at training.
